predecessors.note: The Rohillas settled Katehr under Mughal orders; Ali Muhammad Khan's principality "became independent in 1721" and Muhammad Shah gave him the title of Nawab in 1737 (Ali Mohammed Khan Rohilla page).

land.text: Rohilkhand (Katehr): the subahs of Bareilly, Bijnor, Budaun, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Rampur and Shahjahanpur

successors.note: "Rohilkhand fell to Awadh, and was plundered and occupied" after Miranpur Katra (23 April 1774); Awadh surrendered the whole of Rohilkhand to the East India Company on 10 November 1801.
On 7 October 1774 Faizullah Khan signed the Treaty of Lal Dang and was granted a state of his choosing, which became Rampur State (British protection). rampur-state needs a dossier.

capitals.name: Aonla
capitals.note: "with its seat at Aonla, 18 miles north-west of Bareilly city".

capitals.name: Bareilly
capitals.note: The Rohilkhand page lists Aonla, Bareilly and Rampur as capitals without years and says Bareilly "was made the capital of the Rohilkhand state"; the years here follow the regency of Hafiz Rahmat Khan from 15 September 1748 and are a reading.

rulers.name: Hafiz Rahmat Khan
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: Regent from 15 September 1748 to 23 April 1774, when he was killed at Miranpur Katra.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row. The pages describe the extent only as the subahs of Bareilly, Bijnor, Budaun, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Rampur and Shahjahanpur; the principality of Ali Muhammad Khan in the early years was smaller (a seat at Aonla) and its growth is not dated on the pages, so one region stands for the whole life. Area about 25,000 km2; no infobox area (the infobox gives "1690" as the establishment date).

region.text: the principality with its seat at Aonla, near Bareilly

ledger.note: 1721: Ali Muhammad Khan makes Rohilkhand independent of the Mughals. The Rohilkhand page lists his reign from 1721; "which became independent in 1721"; the title of Nawab came from Muhammad Shah in 1737. The seat was Aonla, "18 miles north-west of Bareilly city".

region.text: the Terai parganas of Kumaon including Kashipur and Rudrapur

ledger.note: 1742: Ali Mohammed Khan annexes parganas of Kumaon. "In 1742 Ali Mohammed Khan of Rohilkhand invaded Kumaon" and annexed several parganas, including Kashipur and Rudrapur (the Kumaon Kingdom page; the Ali Mohammed Khan Rohilla page, opened, is silent on Kumaon). The extent of the parganas is two circles, my reading.

region.text: Rohilkhand (Katehr): the subahs of Bareilly, Bijnor, Budaun, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Rampur and Shahjahanpur

ledger.note: 1772: Mahadji Shinde and the Marathas invade Rohilkhand. He defeated the Rohillas "during 1772-73" and captured Najibabad (no month); the Rohilkhand page has a treaty of 15 June 1772 between Shuja-ud-Daula and Hafiz Rahmat Khan and "In 1773, the Marathas once again crossed the Ganges at Ramghat in Badaun". Najibabad lay in the lands of Najib ud-Daula, not of Hafiz Rahmat.

region.text: Rohilkhand (Katehr): the subahs of Bareilly, Bijnor, Budaun, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Rampur and Shahjahanpur

ledger.note: 1773: the Marathas withdraw. The Rohillas had been "driven into the mountains by the Marathas" (Rohilla War page); the pages give no treaty or day for the end of the Maratha incursion.

region.text: Rohilkhand (Katehr): the subahs of Bareilly, Bijnor, Budaun, Moradabad, Pilibhit, Rampur and Shahjahanpur

ledger.note: 1774: Shuja-ud-Daula, with the East India Company brigade, invades Rohilkhand over the money the Rohillas refused to pay. "The Nawab was supported by troops of the British East India Company"; the infobox runs 1773-1774; the page gives no day for the start.

ledger.note: 23 April 1774: Hafiz Rahmat Khan is killed at Miranpur Katra and Rohilkhand passes to Awadh. "defeated by Colonel Alexander Champion on 23 April 1774 at the Battle of Miranpur Katra"; "Rohilkhand fell to Awadh, and was plundered and occupied."

7 October 1774: Faizullah Khan keeps Rampur. "on 7 October 1774 Faizullah signed an amicable treaty of Lal Dang" and was granted a princely state of his choosing, which became Rampur State; the page does not give its boundary, so the Rampur circle is a reading.

notes: Five pages opened (Rohilkhand, Ali Mohammed Khan Rohilla, Rohilla War, Mahadji Shinde, and Kumaon Kingdom for the 1742 parganas of Kashipur and Rudrapur, which the kumaon-kingdom dossier records as the matching loss). The article "Rohilkhand Kingdom" returned url_not_found; the state has no page of its own among those opened, so wikipedia is given as the region article. Gaps: the 1745 grant of Katehr, the 1745-46 Mughal expedition against Ali Muhammad (page: 1746 altercation, expedition, imprisonment, pardon as governor of Sirhind), Ghulam Qadir (1788) and the early growth of the state are not dated on the pages opened; one region stands for the whole life. The capital move to Bareilly is not dated on the pages. Rohilkhand lay inside Awadh from 1774 and passed to the East India Company on 10 November 1801 (nawab-of-awadh, other group). Counterpart needing a dossier: rampur-state (1774 to 1949). The Rohilkhand infobox gives 1690 as the state's start; the pages do not support it.
